additional_support: Fever ≥38°C: hold both medicines and contact the team; restarting requires the agreed plan after at least 24 hours symptom-free. Recurrent episodes need their own assessment. Dabrafenib is moderate-to-high emetic risk and trametinib minimal-to-low; the combined plan must reflect both.

Discuss fertility and pregnancy precautions before starting. Use an effective alternative to hormonal contraception during treatment and for two weeks after dabrafenib and 16 weeks after trametinib; dabrafenib can make hormonal contraception less effective. The team must confirm the method and the later applicable end date for the combination. Do not breastfeed during treatment; ask when it is safe to resume. Report a possible pregnancy promptly.

Fever is a particular concern. At 38°C or above, withhold both medicines and contact the oncology team promptly under the written fever plan; recurrent episodes may require action at the first symptoms. Infection and dehydration also need assessment. Restart only when the team tells you. Urgent help is also needed for vision change, severe rash, chest pain, breathlessness, bleeding or severe muscle symptoms.
This is not an issued prescription. The clinician and pharmacist must complete and authorise any supportive medicines.
